newsitem.title: USA: Dow overcomes profit-taking to edge to new record.
newsitem.headline: Dow overcomes profit-taking to edge to new record.

text.p: The Dow industrials edged to a new all-time high on Monday, overcoming broad profit-taking among oil shares.
The Dow climbed five points to close unofficially at 6709 after a session devoid of the volatility that has marked trading since the start of the year.
J.P. Morgan & Co Inc turned the strongest performance among Dow components, rising 2-3/4 to 102-1/2 after reporting stronger-than-expected fourth quarter earnings.
The results triggered a bit of a rally in financial shares, but analysts said activity appeared restrained ahead of tomorrow's release of December consumer price data.
Oil shares were the exception, however, falling broadly on a dip in crude prices and a move by investors to realize some profits from the group's recent surge.
"When you start profit-taking you have to go where the profits are," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "Clearly the oil shares have been strong performers lately."
Once again, stocks got little help from the interest rate front, as bonds continued to edge lower. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury eased 3/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
Despite the sustained increase in rates, some analysts saw reason for optimism.
"What stuck out more than anything were the utilities, where we saw some buying," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
Because utilities are viewed as a barometer of interest rate sentiment, he said, "We may be getting our first inkling that rates are topping out."
Crude prices slid $0.90 to $25.19 a barrel in New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) activity, in a technical sell-off that was fueled by forecasts of mild East Coast temperatures.

Elsewhere, the market was noticeably muted and stocks held to fairly tight ranges. Remarkably, the session was the first this year that failed to produce a swings wide enough to trigger the New York Stock Exchange's program trading curbs.
"Today was a moment to breathe," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We still saw evidence that profit-taking is short-lived, shallow and greeted with buyers."
Among financial shares, BankAmerica Corp rose 1-1/4 to 99-1/4 and First Chicago NBD Corp gained 7/8 to 53-3/8.
Among oil shares, Texaco Inc shed 1-3/8 to 106, Exxon Corp slipped 2-5/8 to 103-1/8 and Mobil Corp dipped 2-1/2 to 127-5/8.

In individual issues, Advanced Micro Devices Inc rose 1-3/4 to 29-3/8 ahead of the company's earnings release. After the close, AMD reported a fourth quarter loss of $0.15 per share versus a profit of $0.07 in the comparable period a year ago.
Early in the day, Morgan Stanley started coverage of the company with a rating of outperform, saying it expected AMD to turn profitable in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.

Amgen Inc dipped 2-1/16 to 53, after the shares were downgraded by a pair of Wall Street firms. Last Friday, Amgen and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc announced disappointing results in a Phase III trial of their drug intended to treat Lou Gehrig's disease.
Regeneron shares fell 1-5/8 to 9-3/8.
Broad indices reflected the market's tepid tone.
The S&P 500 index eked out a new all-time high, rising 0.01 to 759.51.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.11 to 1330.91.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
